passages.text: Now about the service to the saints, there is no need for me to write to you.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the church in Corinth.
Paul speaks about the service to the saints.
Paul says he does not need to write to them about this service.
Paul believes they already understand this matter.
passages.original: Περὶ μὲν γὰρ τῆς διακονίας τῆς εἰς τοὺς ἁγίους περισσόν μοί ἐστιν τὸ γράφειν ὑμῖν

passages.text: For I know your eagerness to help, and I have been boasting to the Macedonians that since last year you in Achaia were prepared to give. And your zeal has stirred most of them to do likewise.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter to the church in Corinth.
Paul spoke to the believers in Achaia.
Paul knew that these believers were eager to help.
Paul told the Macedonians about their eagerness.
Paul said that the believers in Achaia were ready to give since last year.
Paul saw that their zeal inspired many others.
Most of the Macedonians wanted to help because of this zeal.
passages.original: οἶδα γὰρ τὴν προθυμίαν ὑμῶν ἣν ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν καυχῶμαι Μακεδόσιν ὅτι Ἀχαΐα παρεσκεύασται ἀπὸ πέρυσι καὶ τὸ ὑμῶν ζῆλος ἠρέθισεν τοὺς πλείονας

passages.text: But I am sending the brothers in order that our boasting about you in this matter should not prove empty, but that you will be prepared, just as I said.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the church in Corinth.
Paul has been boasting to others about the Corinthians' readiness to give.
Paul is sending the brothers to the Corinthians.
He wants to make sure his boasting about them is not empty.
He wants the Corinthians to be prepared.
He wants them to be ready just as he said they would be.
passages.original: Ἔπεμψα δὲ τοὺς ἀδελφούς ἵνα μὴ τὸ καύχημα ἡμῶν τὸ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν κενωθῇ ἐν τῷ μέρει τούτῳ ἵνα καθὼς ἔλεγον παρεσκευασμένοι ἦτε

passages.text: Otherwise, if any Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we—to say nothing of you—would be ashamed of having been so confident.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the believers in Achaia.
Paul has been boasting to the Macedonians about the believers in Achaia.
Paul says, "If any Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we will be ashamed."
Paul means that he and his companions will feel shame for being so confident in the believers.
Paul also means that the believers themselves would be ashamed in this situation.
Paul wants the believers to be ready, so that no one will be embarrassed.
passages.original: μή πως ἐὰν ἔλθωσιν σὺν ἐμοὶ Μακεδόνες καὶ εὕρωσιν ὑμᾶς ἀπαρασκευάστους καταισχυνθῶμεν ἡμεῖς ἵνα μὴ λέγωμεν ὑμεῖς ἐν τῇ ὑποστάσει ταύτῃ

passages.text: So I thought it necessary to urge the brothers to visit you beforehand and make arrangements for the bountiful gift you had promised. This way, your gift will be prepared generously and not begrudgingly.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the Corinthian church.
\r\nPaul wants the Corinthians to be ready to give the gift they promised.
\r\nPaul decided it was necessary to send the brothers to them.
\r\nPaul urged the brothers to visit the Corinthians before he arrived.
\r\nThe brothers will help prepare the promised gift.
\r\nThe gift should be ready when Paul comes.
\r\nThe gift should be given as a blessing.
\r\nThe gift should not be given out of greed or reluctance.
passages.original: ἀναγκαῖον οὖν ἡγησάμην παρακαλέσαι τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ἵνα προέλθωσιν εἰς ὑμᾶς καὶ προκαταρτίσωσιν τὴν προεπηγγελμένην εὐλογίαν ὑμῶν ταύτην ἑτοίμην εἶναι οὕτως ὡς εὐλογίαν καὶ μὴ ὡς πλεονεξίαν

passages.text: Remember this: Whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows generously will also reap generously.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the church in Corinth.
Paul teaches about giving.
Paul says, “Remember this.”
If a person sows sparingly, that person will reap sparingly.
If a person sows generously, that person will reap generously.
passages.original: Τοῦτο δέ ὁ σπείρων φειδομένως φειδομένως καὶ θερίσει καὶ ὁ σπείρων ἐπ’ εὐλογίαις ἐπ’ εὐλογίαις καὶ θερίσει

passages.text: Each one should give what he has decided in his heart to give, not out of regret or compulsion. For God loves a cheerful giver.
passages.sermon:
Each person should decide in his heart what to give.
He should give that amount.
He should not give out of regret.
He should not give because he feels forced.
God loves a cheerful giver.
passages.original: ἕκαστος καθὼς προῄρηται τῇ καρδίᾳ μὴ ἐκ λύπης ἢ ἐξ ἀνάγκης ἱλαρὸν γὰρ δότην ἀγαπᾷ ὁ Θεός

passages.text: And God is able to make all grace abound to you, so that in all things, at all times, having all that you need, you will abound in every good work.
passages.sermon:
God is able to give you all grace.
God can make grace overflow to you.
God gives you everything you need at all times.
You will always have enough.
You will have what you need for every good work.
You will do many good works because God provides for you.
passages.original: δυνατεῖ δὲ ὁ Θεὸς πᾶσαν χάριν περισσεῦσαι εἰς ὑμᾶς ἵνα ἐν παντὶ πάντοτε πᾶσαν αὐτάρκειαν ἔχοντες περισσεύητε εἰς πᾶν ἔργον ἀγαθόν

passages.text: As it is written: “He has scattered abroad His gifts to the poor; His righteousness endures forever.”
passages.sermon:
God gives gifts to the poor.
God spreads these gifts widely.
God’s righteousness lasts forever.
Scripture says this.
passages.original: καθὼς γέγραπται Ἐσκόρπισεν ἔδωκεν τοῖς πένησιν ἡ δικαιοσύνη αὐτοῦ μένει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα

passages.text: Now He who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your store of seed and will increase the harvest of your righteousness.
passages.sermon:
God supplies seed to the sower.
God gives bread for food.
God will supply your seed.
God will multiply your seed.
God will increase the harvest of your righteousness.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἐπιχορηγῶν σπόρον τῷ σπείροντι καὶ ἄρτον εἰς βρῶσιν χορηγήσει καὶ πληθυνεῖ τὸν σπόρον ὑμῶν καὶ αὐξήσει τὰ γενήματα τῆς δικαιοσύνης ὑμῶν

passages.text: You will be enriched in every way to be generous on every occasion, so that through us your giving will produce thanksgiving to God.
passages.sermon:
God will enrich you in every way.
He will do this so you can be generous at all times.
Your generosity will come through us.
Your giving will cause people to thank God.
passages.original: ἐν παντὶ πλουτιζόμενοι εἰς πᾶσαν ἁπλότητα ἥτις κατεργάζεται δι’ ἡμῶν εὐχαριστίαν τῷ Θεῷ

passages.text: For this ministry of service is not only supplying the needs of the saints, but is also overflowing in many expressions of thanksgiving to God.
passages.sermon:
This ministry is a service to others.
This ministry supplies what the saints lack.
This ministry also causes many people to thank God.
This ministry overflows with thanksgiving to God.
passages.original: ὅτι ἡ διακονία τῆς λειτουργίας ταύτης οὐ μόνον ἐστὶν προσαναπληροῦσα τὰ ὑστερήματα τῶν ἁγίων ἀλλὰ καὶ περισσεύουσα διὰ πολλῶν εὐχαριστιῶν τῷ Θεῷ

passages.text: Because of the proof this ministry provides, the saints will glorify God for your obedient confession of the gospel of Christ, and for the generosity of your contribution to them and to all the others.
passages.sermon:
This ministry shows clear proof of your faith.
The saints see this proof.
The saints glorify God because of it.
You obey the gospel of Christ.
You confess your faith in Christ.
You give generously to the saints.
You also give generously to all others.
Your obedience and generosity cause the saints to praise God.
passages.original: διὰ τῆς δοκιμῆς τῆς διακονίας ταύτης δοξάζοντες τὸν Θεὸν ἐπὶ τῇ ὑποταγῇ τῆς ὁμολογίας ὑμῶν εἰς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἁπλότητι τῆς κοινωνίας εἰς αὐτοὺς καὶ εἰς πάντας

passages.text: And their prayers for you will express their affection for you, because of the surpassing grace God has given you.
passages.sermon:
The saints will pray for you.
They will feel deep affection for you.
God has given you surpassing grace.
Their affection comes because of this great grace from God.
passages.original: καὶ αὐτῶν δεήσει ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν ἐπιποθούντων ὑμᾶς διὰ τὴν ὑπερβάλλουσαν χάριν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐφ’ ὑμῖν

passages.text: Thanks be to God for His indescribable gift!
passages.sermon: God gives a gift.\r\nNo one can fully describe this gift.\r\nWe thank God for this gift.
passages.original: Χάρις τῷ Θεῷ ἐπὶ τῇ ἀνεκδιηγήτῳ αὐτοῦ δωρεᾷ
